question: Does the proposed confirmation test hold its size and have useful power on this candidate's own rounded, dependent loss differences? Does 500 origins reach 80% power at 10% skill, and if not, what length does?

procedure_under_test.score: the 23-quantile grid score (scoring_protocol.grid_crps) averaged over h = 1..5 per decision origin, one number per origin
procedure_under_test.claim_A: W_b = 0.97 S_b - S_C per origin and mandatory baseline b. Pass: the simultaneous one-sided 95% lower bound on mean W_b is above zero for every baseline (max-t over the baselines). Fail at the threshold: the one-sided 95% upper bound on mean W_b is below zero for at least one baseline (per baseline, no multiplicity adjustment; a marked point for her). Otherwise inconclusive. Skill is 1 - S_C / S_b, so mean W_b = 0 is exactly 3% skill
procedure_under_test.claim_B: gated: one-sided 5% test that mean (S_flag - S_net) is above zero, run in every simulated data set and read jointly with A as 'A passes and B rejects'
procedure_under_test.bootstrap: stationary block bootstrap of whole origin vectors (all baselines' W together), mean block length ell, each resample studentized by its own Bartlett HAC standard error at lag 50 (scoring_protocol._long_run_variance, the protocol's estimator), t* = (mean* - mean) / se*; the critical value is the 95% quantile of max_b t*_b (A, lower) or of t* (B); per-baseline 5% quantile of t*_b for the upper bound
procedure_under_test.baselines: B1'* (calendar-aware persistence with the corrected horizon, #1388) and B2 (legacy climatology, standing in for the calendar climatology B2*, which is not yet built); legacy B1 is not tested and only its development mean is reported; B4 is not built

data.source: docs/research/confirmation-size-power-1392/losses.json, written by scripts/confirmation_losses_1392.py from the walk of scripts/b1_anchor_horizon_1388.py (the candidate, the announced-flag arm (s3c-ann), B1, B1', B1*, B1'*, B2 at the 18:00 decision instant), the development window (targets to 2025-12-31) and the 2026 development days (to 2026-09-03), concatenated in time order
data.regime_labels: the development window's regime labels of the state-scaled study (2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26); the 2026 window carries none and its origins take 2025-26, and the one unlabelled origin takes the label before it
data.pool: the pooled origins are the empirical population; every origin carries the vector (S_C, S_flag, S_B1'*, S_B2)

schemes.block: a stationary (circular) resample of whole origin vectors from the pool, mean generation block 30 origins (not one of the analysis blocks 20, 50, 100). Population mean skill is exactly the imposed one
schemes.regime: a first-order Markov chain on the regime labels (transition matrix estimated from the label sequence in time order); each step emits an origin of the current regime: the regime's next origin with probability 1 - 1/30 while the state stays, else a fresh draw from that regime. Population mean skill is exactly the imposed one under the chain's stationary law

imposed_skill: each baseline's losses are multiplied by one constant c_b so that 1 - mean(S_C) / mean(c_b S_b) equals the stated skill under the scheme's own population law; the candidate's losses, the rounding, the dependence and the regime structure are the real ones. The announced-flag arm is rescaled the same way for B. Cell group 'observed' leaves the baselines unscaled (the development skill: about +13% against B1'* and +36% against B2 on the development window)

cell_groups.main: both baselines at the same skill 0% (below the threshold: the chance to fail), 3% (the null: size), 5% and 10% (power); test block 50
cell_groups.binding: one baseline at 3% (binding) and the other at 10%, in both orders: size when only one baseline is at the boundary
cell_groups.gated: A at 10% for both baselines and B's skill (net over flag) at 0% (B's null), 1%, 2% and 3%: B's size (unconditional and given that A passed), B's power and the joint probability that A passes and B rejects. The development skill of the net over the flag arm is +0.1% on the development window and +2.4% on the 2026 days
cell_groups.extension: lengths 1000 and 1500 at 10%, to answer 'what length reaches 80% power' if 500 and 750 do not
cell_groups.sensitivity: test blocks 20 and 100 at the three non-null-or-below effects 3%, 5%, 10% (main grid otherwise); the full mode only
cell_groups.binding_observed: B1'* at 3%, 5% or 10% skill and B2 as developed (unscaled; about +36% on the development window), test block 50: what the candidate's real position against B2 does to the pass rate when B1'* is the binding baseline
cell_groups.extension_observed: the same at 10% against B1'* with B2 as developed, at lengths 250..750 (in binding_observed) and 1000, 1500, 2500 (here), to answer the length question for the baseline that binds

reduced.why: what a session can run; M data sets per cell and `reps` bootstrap resamples per data set. A rate p is read with Monte Carlo standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/M), at most 3.5 points; a 5% quantile of 199 draws is the 10th largest, so the critical value itself carries error

full.why: the Mac run (needs-mac): standard error at most 2.2 points; the declared 50,000 resamples of the frozen test are not run inside a size study (50,000 per data set times 500 data sets per cell is beyond any machine here); this run says whether the procedure holds, and its own 50,000-resample use is the same code with a larger `reps`

reading_rules: A rate of passing at 3% skill is the procedure's size at the boundary; a rate within the Monte Carlo interval of 5% or below is read as holding its size, above as over-rejecting. No threshold is set by this study.
Power is the rate of passing at 5% and 10%; 80% is the usual target and is the line this study reports against. It decides nothing.
Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is adopted, and the registered design stays Eleonora's decision.

amendments.what: cell groups binding_observed and extension_observed added, and the lengths 1000, 1500 and 2500 for the latter
amendments.why: the first reduced run (groups main, observed, binding, gated, extension; committed result before this amendment) put the power at 10% skill against both baselines at 23% or less at every length: the long-run variance of W against B2, which the candidate beats by about 36% in development, is several times that against B1'*, so imposing 10% on B2 (a 28% deflation of its losses) makes B2 the binding baseline at every length. That cell group is kept as declared; the added groups hold B2 as developed and impose skill on B1'* alone. Added after the figures of the first run were seen
amendments.computed_before: groups main, observed, binding, gated, extension at M=200, reps=199
